summary: Defines an ALTO service that lets a client get several cost metrics in a single request for filtered cost maps and endpoint cost maps. It also extends the constraints so clients can filter using logical combinations of tests on multiple metrics.

eli5.summary: Instead of asking separately how far, how fast and how cheap, you ask once and get all the answers.

questions: how to request multiple alto cost metrics
subtitle: Ask an ALTO server for several cost metrics in one request, and filter them with AND and OR tests.

tldr.problem: The base ALTO protocol allows only one cost type per cost map or Endpoint Cost request, so a client that cares about several metrics must send several requests.
tldr.mechanism: Filtered Cost Map and Endpoint Cost requests may list several cost types and receive an array of values per entry. Constraints can test any listed metric and be combined with OR as well as AND.
tldr.outcome: A client gets consistent values for several metrics in one transaction, and legacy clients keep working because they ignore the new fields.

today: RFC 8189 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the base protocol of RFC 7285 rather than replacing it.

sections.title: Why Multiple Costs in One Request
sections.content:
ALTO (Application-Layer Traffic Optimization), defined in RFC 7285, gives overlay applications guidance for choosing hosts, using costs between network locations such as "hopcount" and "routingcost". The base protocol allows only one cost type per cost map or Endpoint Cost request, so several metrics need several requests.

The RFC gives three reasons to batch them. One cost map covering N cost types is less bulky than N maps of one type each. It saves round trips and processing on client and server. And values delivered together are consistent, which helps clients that need synchronized updates.

The same applications may need to weigh conflicting goals, so the RFC also extends the constraint tests. The base protocol allows only an AND of comparisons on the one requested cost type. This document adds tests on several metrics combined with OR as well as AND.
sections.eli5: Asking for everything at once is faster than making many trips, and the answers all match up in time.

sections.title: The Multi-Cost Data Format
sections.content:
A cost in an ALTO cost map may be any JSON value, though implementations may assume a JSON number. This document lets a cost be an array of costs, one per metric. A new multi-cost-types member in the response meta lists the metrics, so the client knows which array position means which metric.

The response keeps an empty cost-type member ({}) for backwards compatibility. If a cost type is unavailable for a source and destination, the server MUST use JSON null for that array element. If none are available, the server MAY omit the entry.

Only the Filtered Cost Map and Endpoint Cost Services are extended. A full multi-cost map can be obtained from a filtered cost map resource by omitting the source and destination PIDs.
sections.eli5: Where a table cell used to hold one number, it now holds a short list of numbers, and a header says what each one means.

sections.title: Compatibility with Legacy Clients
sections.content:
No new media types are defined. Instead the Information Resource Directory (IRD) entry of a resource gets a new capability, max-cost-types: the maximum number of cost types the resource can return per request. Its presence tells a client that the resource understands these extensions. If omitted, the default is 0.

Legacy clients ignore unknown fields, as RFC 7285 requires, so they keep sending the cost-type parameter and get a normal single-valued cost map. A multi-cost-aware client sends multi-cost-types instead, and the server answers with array-valued costs in that order. A client MUST specify either cost-type or multi-cost-types, never both, and MUST NOT use multi-cost-types unless max-cost-types is greater than 0.

A second capability, testable-cost-type-names, restricts constraint tests to a subset of cost-type-names. It is mutually exclusive with cost-constraints being true, so a legacy client sees such a resource as having no constraint support and cannot issue tests on untestable metrics.
sections.eli5: Old clients do not know about the new feature and simply keep asking the old way. New clients use the new way and the server can tell them apart.

sections.title: Request and Response Parameters
sections.content:
The filtered cost map request (ReqFilteredCostMap) gains these optional fields: multi-cost-types, testable-cost-types, constraints and or-constraints. The Endpoint Cost request gets the same additions.

The multi-cost-types entries must match cost-type-names of the resource, and the list must not exceed max-cost-types. Even a single cost type in this field produces arrays with one value.

In the response, meta carries multi-cost-types with the same value as the request. Every array has the same length as that list and holds the values in that order.

The Endpoint Cost Service response follows the same pattern as the filtered cost map response.
sections.eli5: You fill in a form saying which measurements you want. The answer comes back in the same order you asked.

sections.title: Extended Constraint Tests
sections.content:
A constraint predicate now has the form [#] op value, where the optional index selects a cost metric. The default is [0], so legacy tests such as le 10 remain valid. The index refers to testable-cost-types if present, otherwise to multi-cost-types, otherwise to the single cost-type (index 0).

The or-constraints field is an array of arrays of predicates: the OR of ANDs. A cost point is returned only if it satisfies all predicates of at least one inner array. It MUST NOT contain an empty inner array, and it cannot be used together with constraints. A plain constraints list is equivalent to an or-constraints value with one inner array.

With testable-cost-types a client can filter on a metric it does not want returned. For example, it can ask for routingcost only for pairs whose hopcount is within a limit, which the RFC likens to a database query that selects one column with a condition on another.
sections.eli5: You can say "show me trips that are either short and cheap, or a bit longer but very cheap", and the server filters for you.

sections.title: Privacy, Security and IANA
sections.content:
The document defines no new media types and has no new IANA considerations. It says it introduces no privacy or security issues beyond those already present in ALTO. Multi-cost requests tend to reduce on-the-wire volume compared with several single-cost transactions, and multi-cost constraints further filter server responses.

The RFC does note one privacy point: queries for multiple metrics are a stronger fingerprinting signal than queries for one metric, so implementations may leak more information about the client. It adds that in many cases queries could already be linked by the source IP address or other existing information.
sections.eli5: Asking many questions at once makes you easier to recognize, but people could often tell it was you anyway.

cells: An array, one value per listed cost type
AND, or OR of ANDs via or-constraints
